6/4/25 Catalog Meeting - https://app.fireflies.ai/view/EuroContempo-Allmoxy-Custom-Cabinet-Work::01JWVJCJD2J2GWK64W24SVVPYJ Agenda: Assembled pricing Finished Interiors Validations Corrected Next Steps? Ray to finish the assembled and finished interior pricing. Neil to review and confirm if the product is ready for cloning Determine how we want to tackle cloning Move onto the CV ORD export file configuration Notes: Question Is everything pricing correctly as is now? (Ray sharing) Assembled Questions Meeting Summary The team reviewed updates made to the Allmoxy cabinet configurator, focusing on assembly logic, UI validation improvements, and pricing calculations. Ray implemented several fixes based on issues shared earlier by Neil, particularly around selection inputs, pricing visibility, and configuration logic. Discussion also covered pricing structure for assembled cabinets, handling of hinge/glide types, inclusion of hardware and accessory options, and future enhancements such as cubic feet calculations for logistics. Key Takeaways Important Discussions Updated the “Assembled” input from a checkbox to a dropdown with clearer options: Flatpack and Assembled. Default state now requires explicit selection to avoid pricing omissions and configuration inconsistencies. Clarified terminology in UI: changed duplicate “Hinge Drilling” labels to Hinge Type and Glide Type for better end-user clarity. New accessory insert options (e.g., trash can pullouts, lazy susans) added to base products and tied to assembled state. Revised validation logic for door styles and vertical/horizontal selections—several now working correctly. Solid no grain option added for both doors and drawer fronts with corresponding validations. Allmoxy is set to calculate and show proper pricing based on current inputs and logic layers. Proposed solution: separate TFL and veneer materials into distinct tables to reduce validation complexity and improve maintainability. Large attribute tables and the need for frequent overrides led to the decision to split material tables. Concern over customer confusion due to too many dropdown options and validation errors if all materials are shown. Assembly pricing needs to accommodate variability in cabinet complexity without overcomplicating setup. Determine a strategy for assigning assembly multipliers and flat charges for each cabinet category/type. Add and test Box Construction logic with dropdowns for “Flat Pack” and “Fully Assembled” selections. Set up assembly pricing formulas (multiplier, flat fee) based on Neil’s forthcoming inputs. Edge Banding Specifics: Carson emphasized that edge banding on cabinet sides (left/right) must account for both face and bottom edges (i.e., both long and short axes), differing from Allmoxy's current single-axis logic. Static Dimensions: Some parts like stretchers and nailers have fixed dimensions regardless of cabinet size and need to be hardcoded in the system. Component Relevance by Cabinet Type: Carson outlined which parts apply to specific cabinet types (e.g., base, wall, tall), highlighted in his spreadsheet. Incorporate dual-axis edge banding where needed. Add missing waste and markup logic to edge banding. Continue using the spreadsheet as a reference to validate Allmoxy logic alignment. engagements.body: See Churn playbook and retention notes for full context. For more information reach out to the former assigned CSM.

Churn Playbook Please select all of the reasons that apply for why the customer is churning. Add any additional churn context in the note - the more the better here. If there's escalation notes that exist on the account be sure to reference them and include the data of the escalation note in the playbook context. Features, Moved to Other Solution Notes: Key Takeaways Important Discussions Kurt confirmed that they will be switching back to Drawer Lister due to unresolved challenges with Allmoxy’s production and reporting tools. Key frustration stemmed from the plant schedule and lack of accurate daily totals, which hindered delivery planning and overloaded their delivery vehicles. Communication breakdowns were highlighted — notably, there was no contact from Allmoxy between May 21st and July 28th, despite unresolved issues. Kurt emphasized that while Allmoxy’s front-end order entry experience is strong, the back-end manufacturing support falls short for their needs. Kurt's team had to outsource shop sheets, which led to confusion and inefficiency on the production floor. Complexity and customization of their products made implementation difficult — Zach had done extensive development that was not fully supported by Allmoxy’s engineering team. Allmoxy acknowledged these issues and shared that the internal development focus had shifted this summer away from key manufacturing features. Sarah and Josh acknowledged Allmoxy had not met expectations but reaffirmed their commitment to developing these features for future benefit. Technical Issues & Fixes Production scheduling and plant schedule functionality were lacking and caused daily operational inefficiencies. Shop sheet generation was insufficient — required third-party development, resulting in confusion and limited adoption on the production floor. Back-end limitations undermined the value of the system despite strong order entry capabilities. Invoice and acknowledgment formatting issues led to customer backlash and loss of clients due to unclear or incorrect order information. Lack of order summation and total calculation tools hindered efficient planning. Change the Customer Lifecycle property to "Other" and create a task for Kylie to review after 1 year. Customer

Kurt’s team expressed significant frustration over key production and reporting features that Allmoxy did not support, prompting their decision to revert to Drawer Lister. Sarah and Josh acknowledged the issues, clarified internal development prioritization problems, and expressed a strong interest in retaining the relationship in the future. The conversation remained respectful, with both sides agreeing to keep communication open and data preserved for a potential return. Decisions Made Kurt’s team will officially cancel Allmoxy by December 20, 2025, with the final billing to run on November 20, 2025, covering service through December 20. Allmoxy’s engineering team lacks consistency in experience and domain expertise, which affected the buildout for specialty manufacturing customers. The product is not currently viable for manufacturers with complex, custom backend workflows. Action Items Josh to send Kurt's team the cancellation form with optional detail submission. Sarah to share parts of the meeting with leadership and development team as feedback and to advocate for prioritizing missing features. Big Valley Wood 4/3/25 Meeting Summary This meeting served as a final planning and alignment session to support the customer's transition from their legacy system to Allmoxy, targeting full cutover by April 18. The team reviewed critical checklist items related to batch order workflows, output formatting, and visibility needs for production. A primary goal was to design a workflow that replaces the customer's current plant schedule with a custom batch export in Allmoxy, ensuring it is easy to use, totals drawer counts, and hides pricing for floor visibility. Discussions also included label setup, order report customization, timestamp issues, and output page sorting. Additional enhancements, such as implementing a code switcher for output page types and reusing formatted HTML, were explored to maintain consistency. Key Takeaways Important Discussions The customer's legacy system is being phased out, with complete retirement scheduled for April 18. Production is currently running in parallel. The current plant schedule is a printed report used by all departments. The team aims to replicate this in Allmoxy using the "Batch Orders" tool and a custom CSV export. The batch report provides line-level detail and drawer piece counts, but lacks a total count summary, which is essential for planning. This solution should eliminate the need for the "Scheduled Capacity" feature. Technical Issues & Fixes The batch orders view does not currently total drawer counts; this may be addressed with a CSV export or UI enhancement (e.g., pop-up total). The order report reveals pricing, which needs to be hidden for production use. Output page sorting by height/width is inconsistent. Items do not appear in the same order as entered. Onboarding #2 Big Valley To review They do not want customers creating accounts, they would like to create accounts for them (and give login information) Theme looks good Any issues adding employees, or giving permissions? Is Stripe set up? Today we are talking about Tags, Price Adjustments, and Triggers. We are also going to do some live testing to see how things look right now. Tags These are ways you can group customers together for a certain purpose These can be referenced in triggers and price adjustments Ex. you have a group of customers that are cabinet shops, and they get a certain discount. You can give this group of customers a "cabinet shop" tag on their company profile that can then be referenced later. You can also put tags on products How do you think you might group certain customers together? Price Adjustments Do you have customers that are priced differently than others? Why? Use price adjustments to achieve this Say you have a customer that is your oldest and most loyal customer, you always give them a 10% discount no matter what. Price adjustments are basically discounts or surcharges that can be applied to customers, groups of customers, or products. They are adjusted PER ITEM, not the total order amount Priority For when there are multiple price adjustments competing with one another If one discount has a higher priority than the other, the highest priority will override the other discount Ex. if you have a new customer discount and a summer sale discount going on at the same time, you would want the new customer discount to have a higher accumulate than the other. Tip: Use the Always setting, so you know if you are discounting or surcharging every time. You can also discount customers or products with certain tags Triggers How are you currently interacting with customers? Is it manual calls, emails, etc? Triggers can automate that process for you Notify you, and your customers of something happening in Allmoxy Triggers to edit: 1, 6, 12, 16, 18, 19 Does he want to be notified of a bid? Or an order? They also discussed operational workload challenges and plans for follow-up testing and collaboration. Key Takeaways Important Discussions Clarification of email confusion regarding a previous file sent on 5/22; resolved and forwarded. Folder structure and naming cleanup was implemented to isolate and identify materials correctly (e.g., separating Pharaoh, Ingrain, Shade). File naming inconsistencies (e.g., extra spaces in names, missing attributes) were flagged as causes of export/import failures. Material misidentifications observed: Atlantico, Bianco, and Perla coming through as Crystal High Gloss. Pharaoh entries coming through as Razio or Urban White. engagements.body: 11/22 Meeting Prep Notes: Current operation - Rehau receives an order from a customer which they decide they want Reid to manufacture. Rehau takes the export file, fabrication order, and packing slip, screenshot of the resource allocation tab, and their own internal purchase order file and attaches these to an email they send manually to Reid. What we're trying to solve: Automate the transfer of information (order details, export, etc) A place to manage these Rehau orders (inside Reid's allmoxy) Allow Reid to offer Rehau's products in their instance without it pushing the orders through the Rehau's instance (b2b connection) What are our options: Data transfer - we can set up a trigger on Rehau's side to automatically send the order data and attachments to Reid. (only thing that wouldn't be automated is Rehau's purchase order) Order Import - It's possible to build an export that captures Rehau's order data and import that into Reid's instance. (somewhat manual as the customer information has to be entered manually) Allow Reid to offer Rehau's products - Rehau's products must live within Reid's instance, these either have to be built manually or we can technically clone Rehau's products to your instance but we'll lose all of the catalog data that's been built up until this point. Absolutes: For an export to work (instance to instance) the products would have to match exactly The only way to "resell" Rehau's products would be through B2B which you wouldn't be able to edit the products If we copy Rehau's instance into yours you'll lose all of the past product data (Clean slate that replaces everything) Notes: Bryce - joining in a few minutes Catalog Data - is there a way to save their catalog data? Determined a plan of action What we're going to do: We will be keeping the existing Reid catalog and need to expand the currently built Rehau product line within Reid's instance. The expanded products must match exactly what's in Rehau. Set up training on how to build a Rehau product within Reid's instance, using the newer method which includes proxy variables. Modify the currently built export to work within Reid's instance (eventually)

11/15 Meeting - Steve and Bryce Agenda: Export/Rehau updates Aaron working on, he'll confirm once he's completed and ready for testing B2B Show how to connect - Bryce can set this up Will allow us to start selling from Reid once the Rehau work is completed Bryce & Steve's thoughts? Notes: Reid's desired behavior for using Allmoxy Rehau receives an order from their instance and determines they want Reid as the manufacturer Rehau sends the order information over to Reid Reid can import the order information into their Allmoxy instance It can generate all of the desired paperwork/exports Roadblocks Can't import an order from Rehau into Reid's instance without having Rehau's catalog cloned inside of Reid. Rehau would need to have Reid set up as the "Allmoxy supplier" through B2B and then this connection could work but Rehau wouldn't ever do that. Resource allocation and supply management wouldn't be possible without having the catalogs duplicated. Any time Rehau makes an update to their catalog the exact same update would need to happen in Reid's "cloned" catalog. First Steps Get the export for Cabinet Vision working with Reid's CV and from the orders generated by Rehau Need a trigger setup within Rehau to send Reid the necessary paperwork (export, fabrication order, packing slip) Unable to attach the supply allocation but isn't necessary right now Unable to attach Rehau's PO for Reid to do the fabrication Second Step Determine and outline what is possible and isn't possible Use B2B? (most likely not, doesn't solve the problem) Clone Rehau's catalog into Reid? - Could potentially work but someone would have to maintain any updates that Rehau makes.

Julian Woods LLC Julian Woods LLC December 19, 2025 9:00 AM MST 64 mins bobby@allmoxy.com madison@allmoxy.com jaya.krishna@julianwoods.com View Meeting Recording Production Order and Output Page Customization The team confirmed that Almoxy’s output pages can be tailored to match the simplicity and clarity of the current Handsome system’s production orders to improve usability and reduce redundant data (00:08). Phillip Kim and JayaKrishna highlighted missing key attributes such as font size, door side (left/right), finish details, and color categories in Almoxy’s production order outputs compared to Handsome’s system (08:14). Madison Theisen explained that output pages are highly customizable, with adjustable font sizes and attribute displays, but increasing font size reduces the number of products per page (12:40). Bobby Lewis noted that many current output pages contain redundant repeated information, and removing such data would free space for larger fonts and more cabinets per page (13:19). The team agreed that order-level information should appear once at the top, not repeated per cabinet, freeing space for cabinet-specific details like hardware (14:15). Adding color categories specifying wood type (maple or cherry) to cabinet labels is feasible by updating or creating new label attributes in the catalog (27:00). The group clarified that custom drawing orders can be attached as files to orders and shown as internal-use products in Almoxy, but attachments do not print on production orders—they must be accessed separately (16:40). This workflow allows the production team to reference custom drawings during manufacturing without cluttering the printed output pages (19:09). Overall, Madison and Bobby emphasized that output page layout customization is extensive but requires time and collaboration during implementation and training, which will be provided under contract (23:10). Production Process Tracking and Automation Almoxy supports real-time scanning and labor process tracking integrated with barcode scanning to automate production status updates, similar to the current Google Sheets automation (29:45). Bobby Lewis confirmed that Almoxy’s system can track multiple labor steps such as pull out, staining, spraying, sanding (twice), top coating, assembly, and shipping, updating status live as operators scan barcodes (30:22). The system supports barcode scanning per order, per cabinet, and per production station, enabling granular tracking of each step and worker involved (36:30). Barcodes can be configured to submit multiple fields automatically (station, user, order, etc.) to speed up scanning and reduce errors (37:21). Almoxy offers integration options via API or Zapier to push scan data into external tools like Google Sheets for real-time visibility, with Zapier recommended for ease of use (30:50). The team noted that internal technical expertise is needed for API integration, but Almoxy can suggest external consultants if required (33:11). Bobby assured that the system is always live with no downtime or scanning pauses, ensuring continuous production without data loss even if temporary connectivity issues arise (48:00). Phillip Kim raised concerns about data lost during potential system outages, but Bobby confirmed Almoxy’s real-time updates prevent such losses and no scanning pauses occur (48:05). The labor processes feature includes setting up production steps and scanning stations with corresponding barcodes; scanning triggers update order progress and can send automated notifications like customer alerts upon job completion (49:10). A shipping report shows which items have not yet been scanned complete, helping production managers monitor outstanding tasks (50:42). Pricing and Catalog Engineering Almoxy can support complex pricing formulas and adjustments down to the penny, but this requires detailed catalog engineering by specialized engineers (52:10). Bobby Lewis emphasized that Almoxy’s pricing engine can handle variable price formulas based on size, product options, and other variables, but formulas must be properly configured (53:30). Madison clarified that price issues and formula updates are engineering tasks not solved instantly on calls but handled by dedicated implementation engineers (52:54). The team agreed that engineering efforts are critical to replicating and improving pricing accuracy currently managed by Handsome (53:51). Implementation Process and Support Structure The next steps after contract signing involve setting up a clear ownership model between the customer team and Almoxy’s engineering and support resources to ensure smooth implementation (54:00). Madison outlined two main support channels: billable implementation engineers ($150/hour) for catalog and formula setup, and general product training from customer success managers like herself and Sarah (54:13). JayaKrishna is expected to lead internal efforts coordinating with Almoxy’s engineers (54:40). Almoxy can help with training on core system features like triggers and integrations, but configuring external tools like Google Sheets requires customer involvement (55:30). Madison stressed the importance of consistent communication and stable points of contact on both sides to avoid delays and confusion during the project (42:28). The team discussed adding a numeric pick list field next to accessories to track quantities needed per order, which is possible through customization (55:55). Material Requirements Planning (MRP) and Inventory Management Almoxy supports resource allocation and MRP workflows, but these require engineering setup to tie product orders to supply lists and inventory thresholds (57:40). Bobby explained that the resource allocation feature can be configured to generate supply lists for purchase orders based on confirmed orders (58:00). The system can handle minimum and maximum inventory levels and ordering quantities per supply item, enabling automated material planning (58:26). Engineering will define how supplies are allocated per product and variable to ensure accurate MRP outputs matching current business needs (58:54). Data Retention and System Reliability Almoxy is a cloud-based system with unlimited data storage and historical access, enabling retrieval of order and production data for at least one year or longer as needed (39:01). Bobby confirmed there is no cap on data storage, supporting retrieval of detailed production and order history (39:14). Madison noted that data accuracy depends on consistent use and maintenance of the system by the customer team (39:33). The support team will respond quickly to bugs or issues, with escalation processes involving screen recordings and direct developer attention (41:00). Average resolution times vary based on issue complexity, but Almoxy’s support team is highly responsive and reliable according to Bobby and Madison (41:30). Churn Playbook Please select all of the reasons that apply for why the customer is churning. Add any additional churn context in the note - the more the better here. If there's escalation notes that exist on the account be sure to reference them and include the data of the escalation note in the playbook context. Features, Failed Implementation Notes: 1. Implementation & Development Process Breakdown Expectation: David anticipated a collaborative, phased catalog build — developing and reviewing product sections one at a time (e.g., walls, then bases, etc.). Reality: The build process, primarily handled by Juan, was executed as a full catalog all at once with minimal discussion or review until after completion. Impact: This approach caused significant delays, inefficient reviews, and eroded confidence early in the project. The perceived “black box” style of development led to frustration and loss of trust. 2. Inadequate Quoting Capabilities for Sales Team Major Concern: Sales reps could only generate quotes at list pricing, with no built-in mechanism to adjust or factor pricing to stay competitive with dealers. Process Gap: To generate competitive quotes, reps had to manually calculate discount factors outside the system, relying on Excel-based tools — defeating the purpose of a digital platform. Outcome: Sales team was confused, lacked confidence in the tool, and couldn't effectively quote or win business, making Allmoxy ineffective for a core business need. 3. Lack of Internal Confidence Across Teams Customer Service Issues: Carla (Customer Service Manager) had to manually verify and correct product configurations post-order due to catalog inconsistencies. This created extra workload and delayed adoption. Sales Team Pushback: When introduced to the tool, the sales team did not feel confident using it, largely due to quoting limitations and confusion during the rollout. Leadership Confidence Lost: Without internal buy-in from customer service or the sales organization, David felt he couldn’t confidently endorse or mandate Allmoxy’s use. Change the Customer Lifecycle property to "Other" and create a task for Kylie to review after 1 year. Other Additional properties: Pipeline

engagements.title: Churned customer re-engagement consideration
engagements.body: See Churn playbook and retention notes for full context. For more information reach out to the former assigned CSM.

Churn Playbook Please select all of the reasons that apply for why the customer is churning. Add any additional churn context in the note - the more the better here. If there's escalation notes that exist on the account be sure to reference them and include the data of the escalation note in the playbook context. Moved to Other Solution, Paid and Never Used Notes: Customer churning. They are a gym membership customer paying 600/ month with no ROI (they are always too busy to get Allmoxy up and running). We offered a subscription pause and a few hours of implementation on the house and they still don't want to move forward. Total spend on Allmoxy was 24,000. IF this is the customers main/only instance that's churning, change the Customer Lifecycle property(company property) to "Other." DO NOT DO THIS if this is a second instance and the churn does not completely eliminate their status as a customer. Other What's the catalog implementation status? No

Churn Risk Playbook Please share the most up to date health pulse from the CSM's perspective. Red(this customer is not in good standing and is on track to churn) Has this customer asked to pause or cancel their account or is this playbook being utilized preemptively? Requested to pause Notes: Summary: Gym membership customer, never launched and paying around 600 a month for no ROI. Not really on us but he needs to make a decision to keep Allmoxy or find something else. This is one I think we can save! Meeting Summary The client expressed significant concerns about the lack of return on investment from their ongoing use of Allmoxy, having spent approximately $24,000 with little to no revenue generated. They indicated dissatisfaction with its capabilities compared to a full MRP/ERP system and are considering pausing the subscription while they reevaluate their technology stack and operational needs. A pause is being requested, and both parties agreed to reconnect after the holidays to assess the potential future of the partnership. Key Takeaways Important Discussions The client has invested $24,000 into Allmoxy with minimal tangible ROI and is currently paying $600/month. They originally hoped to use Allmoxy as a sales tool and for stock product management but now feel it falls short as a full MRP solution. The client’s CFO advised pausing Allmoxy usage as there's no immediate revenue opportunity, and internal resources are limited. The client emphasized the need for a single system for manufacturing to avoid inefficiencies caused by running multiple platforms. Technical Issues & Fixes The client requires advanced job-level time tracking (e.g., scan-in/scan-out) which their current system doesn't support. They are currently using barcode scanners for inventory but are evaluating broader MRP options. Allmoxy’s functionality is seen as geared more towards basic stock products than custom manufacturing processes. Allmoxy's integration capabilities with Zapier and webhooks were discussed as potential solutions for interoperability with other platforms (e.g., Katana MRP, QuickBooks Online). The automation webinar scheduled for next week was recommended, especially for the client’s tech lead to attend. Decisions Made The rep will advocate for a 2-month pause (January & February), understanding the financial and operational context. The client’s in-house tech team member will review the automation webinar to evaluate future integration paths. Both sides agreed to reconnect after the holidays to reassess direction and alignment with Allmoxy. Challenges or Concerns Pricing in the current Allmoxy catalog is outdated and may be impacting profitability. Client feels the platform isn’t currently providing sufficient value to justify continued monthly costs. Client is considering multiple tools (Katana, QuickBooks Online, Tama) and is unsure if Allmoxy can remain part of the stack. Concern about continued payment without corresponding business value or usage. Action Items Allmoxy rep to submit a request for a pause on billing, ideally covering January and February. Client's tech team member to attend the Allmoxy automation webinar. Implementation team to potentially provide 1–2 free hours to review product catalog, pricing, and attributes. Allmoxy team to review client’s current product offerings and pricing setup. Both teams to discuss possible integration with Katana MRP if supported by Zapier. Next Steps Rep to follow up next week on the pause request status and confirm the final duration. After the holiday season, schedule a strategy session to: Review implementation progress and any necessary system adjustments. Reassess the value of continuing Allmoxy usage. Explore system integration options to support job tracking, costing, and inventory management. Client to internally evaluate the future tech stack (QuickBooks, Tama, Katana, etc.) and decide whether Allmoxy can still fit within the broader strategy. How much is the customers monthly subscription? Please note if the customer has received any reductions in MRR during their lifetime with Allmoxy as well as any significant, recent implementation costs. $598.80 Industry Segment (Data Confirmation) Custom Cabinet Shop Business Size (Data Confirmation) SMB How long have they been a customer of Allmoxy? 01/24/2022 Is this customer launched? No Is this customer working with our implementation team now, if so please elaborate on the nature of the work/project. No Is this customer a legacy/strategic account? No Has the customer proposed any solutions that would eliminate or delay their churn risk? This could be a price reduction or delivery on a specific feature. Notes: Yes, they are a gym membership customer paying ~600 month since 2022. (20,000) They want to pause and re-engage with our team to see what they can do to get their products to where they need to be. Currently everything is pricing really low. Please share any other strategic context that we should consider related to this account. (Ex. Industry influence/connections, personality details, known expansion opportunity, competitor tech stack, etc.) Notes: He hired a new technical person that will help with building automations to other software (Katana) Who's the main customer contact associated with this escalation? We can use validations in the catalog build, meaning, if product A has this selection then only these selections can be made, etc. You can save as bid and ordered since you're labeled as an employee Verified - Once an order has been submitted and reviewed by you or your team it can be moved to a verified status (Ready to build) Which locks the order from changes on the customer side. You can auto-verify if preferred You can use the work schedule report to manage the jobs you're running (once started this moves orders into in-progress) Shipped - You can use the shipping report to mark items as shipped if needed for tracking purposes. Additional notes: Payments - Can happen anytime depending on how you set this up Progress - Customers can receive updates depending on how much you set up. engagements.title: Build out Thermofoil Doors
engagements.body:
When a customer calls us for thermal foiled products, we typically need the following:

1) Door Style

2) Door Size for each door

3) Thermal Foil color choice (attached) need the full list and pricing on there

4) Do they want hinges bored? What type? How many? Hole placement? We provide hinges?

5) Color matched backs? Closest back? White back? Black back?

We also provide other thermal foil products.

1) 1/4 - 3/4 panels flat press 1 side all edges (1.5 inches wide by 96 inches long is the smallest)

2) 1/4 - 3/4 panels 2 sided no edges

3) 1/4 - 3/4 panels custom shapes and sizes

4) 1/4 - 3/4 panels full wrap (closest back, white, black, color matched?)

Currently we would like to offer:

1) 15-20 door styles

2) Ability to request a custom door style

3) Edge Profile default choice (1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 3/8)

4) Ability to add as many doors/panels as necessary

5) Ability to customize edge profile on any door (so default edge when door style is chosen, but can change edge on any door necessary and it overrides default)

6) Ability to change color/texture on a per door/panel basis.

7) Thermal foil color/texture automatically changes sqft pricing appropriately. (ie. solid colors are cheaper than gloss etc.)

engagements.title: Next Steps: The Cabinet Face — 2026-07-01
engagements.body:
- Action the April 28 recommendation: reach out to Kyle/Jessica about keeping their data, then formally cancel if not interested.
- No further implementation effort warranted -- this has been a non-launch for years across multiple attempts.

Onboarding Status Never fully launched despite years of effort (customer since 2019/2020). Long history of struggling to get live orders flowing -- original catalog build was wrong, 3D designer never worked for their retail/direct-to-consumer model, multiple retention/hand-holding attempts over the years. Paused payments in Nov 2024 for a 3-month grace period that was never followed up on. As of April 28, 2026, Allmoxy's own team flagged: "these guys aren't paying and haven't logged in in 2 years, let's just see if they are interested in keeping their data, but otherwise fully cancel them out." Last Touchpoint Most recent direct contact: Nov 21-22, 2024 retention call (Kyle, Broc, Carson) -- agreed to a payment pause Nov 2024-Jan 2025 with a plan to reconnect in January to finish remaining implementation (~20 hours of work estimated at the time). No evidence that January reconnection ever happened. Internal note April 28, 2026 confirms no login in 2 years and recommends cancellation. Last Action Item Owner: Allmoxy. Per the April 28, 2026 internal note, the recommended next step is to check whether Kyle/Jessica want to retain their data, then formally cancel if not. This has not yet been actioned as of this audit. Use Case & Launch Readiness The Cabinet Face wanted a direct-to-consumer cabinet ordering system, but the platform's direction (and their own limited hands-on capacity -- Kyle relied heavily on Jessica) never lined up well with that goal. Effectively never launched in any sustained way across ~5-6 years as a customer. Sources Checked HubSpot (14 notes spanning 2020-2026, clearly showing chronic non-launch and the April 2026 internal recommendation to cancel). Given how recent and unambiguous the internal note is, did not do further Fireflies/Gmail/Jira digging. Flag: This is a clear-cut churn/cleanup case, already identified internally in April but not yet actioned. Recommend closing it out rather than treating as an active account.
@Carson Ward these guys aren't paying and haven't logged in in 2 years, let's just see if they are interested in keeping their data, but otherwise fully cancel them out

engagements.title: Call with Kyle Kwiatkowski
engagements.body:
Kyle has requested to put his account on pause for a few months due to slow business and the inability to market as much as they'd like. I spoke with Jess Ampleman who is doing their buildout and she said there isn't anything they are waiting on Allmoxy for to propel them forward.


After speaking with Broc, we agreed to offer a free two-month pause with the acknowledgment that they would move into an agreement. I provided the first 2 at no cost and the remaining 10 at $300 per-month. Additionally, I went over the new pricing model and what it typically looks like for customers. Kyle was hesitant to sign an agreement as he still doesn't know if he is going to get a functioning system. He understandably doesn't want to get locked in only to find out that Allmoxy won't work for them.


Kyle has put in about 30k into the system over 5 years and still hasn't used it, he said he was "promised the world" when they signed up for Allmoxy. When Kyle initially approached Beau about Allmoxy he said he wanted to create a direct-to-consumer system. They have put much effort into the system which hasn't yielded high results. A part of it has to do with the slowness of the season and the service they are providing to their customers but from what Kyle said they have been hitting a lot of roadblocks with their build-out.  I asked if they have a realistic timeline for launch and he said he is completely unsure. Kyle said he still doesn't know if it will turn out well for a DTC system. This was interesting info to hear because when we spoke over the phone initially he said there was nothing Allmoxy was doing to hold them back from launching/Jess said we didn't need to do anything on our end. So those things don't align with what Kyle had mentioned on our call.


I let him know it might be a good idea to have a expectations realignment/strategy meeting with Kyle, Jess, Carson, and whoever else makes sense to figure out what the best next steps are. The next subscription payment comes out on the 25th. If we could meet before then that would be ideal. Kyle also requested if we don't meet before then that we waive this month's payment.


Next steps:


Kenzi is going to get with Carson on this situation and figure out who makes sense to involve in a meeting for the best next steps and expectations regarding alignment.

Premier Custom Millwork - Cancellation Meeting Takeaway 1/2/25 Context: After Jesse's initial request to cancel, Sarah and I scheduled time with him to discuss the main obstacles he presented in hopes to keep him from wanting to cancel. His original objections were the cost & time for services work, the remaining product lines that would need to be completed for full system usage, and pricing flexibility. 01/02/25 Meeting Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/view/Premier-Custom-Millwork-Allmoxy::z4BqlC8hMtM2uzwe Throughout the conversation with Jesse, Sarah and I got a lot more insight into these issues: Services Cost & Time - His catalog doesn't have all of the products he would need to run both sides of his business and the lift it would take to get this implemented is beyond what he's able to do right now. Custom Door & Millwork businesses - Each of his businesses operate off of his current system (excel pricing sheet) and he doesn't want to manage two separate systems. From Jesse's view the time and energy it would take to move both businesses to using Allmoxy would be at least another year or more. Bandwidth - Jesse has tried to implement Allmoxy Since October of 2022 and hasn't been able to get there partially due to his own lack of time. He'll get into a sprint and we'll make some progress but then he'll go silent for a few months and then we try to pick up the pieces again. He recognizes this falls on him. We asked Jesse what his thoughts are on tabling Allmoxy and doing a short-term pause (3 months) and then revisiting or if the lift is too great to just cancel as a whole. Jesse felt that it'd be better to just cancel. Contract Status: Monthly payments - $899 on 13th of each month Payment history - Never missed a payment in the 27 months since signing Total Paid: (Oct 22' - Dec 24') Subscription: $23,624 Services: $16,911 Total: $40,535 Since Jesse is still technically under contract until May he would need to pay out the remaining 75% of his contract amount which would be $2,967. However, after discussing with Sarah, our thoughts are that we should wave this cancellation fee since he's been so consistent with payment and still never got any value from utilizing the Allmoxy system. I think this would go a long way for Jesse and show that we truly do care about our customers. @Madison Theisen @Beau Lewis - please let me know how we should proceed with Jesse's request and what should come of the remaining 4 months. @Sarah Pierce for vis.

Retention Meeting 1/2/25 (Sarah, Carson, and Jesse) Context: Jesse requested to cancel his Allmoxy account and shared these main objections as to why: Due to the $150/per hour service fees the time needed to build out the rest of our product lines the limitations in flexibility of pricing (aka - freeform pricing) Jesse is still under contract until May so he would still owe Jan - Apr ($3,600) Goal: Have Allmoxy train his in-house technical person how to build/edit products so he can get the benefits from Allmoxy and without wasting additional investment. (cancellation fee 75% contract amount $$2700) Agenda: Better understand the obstacles Jesse shared Present recommended route - training someone that works directly for Jesse to operate his Allmoxy catalog Secure a action plan for next steps needed Notes: Delivery vehicle broke down - everyday something comes up Pricing Flexibility Issue with shipping was taxed - has been resolved Pricing structure - daily basis (seat of their pants pricing - Adding percentages to certain line items on an order) Pull back on moving forward wants to go all in or all out (doesn't want to sit between two systems) Door side Every time there's an issue they don't want to have to bring Juan or services back into the fold. Feedback New they didn't fit the exact business model Layout template In discussing with Jesse the challenges he's faced over the last 2+ years in trying to launch, it came down to the following items: Managing two systems - doesn't want to manage two systems but in his view it would take at least another year to build out and set up the catalog to meet the needs of his two businesses (custom doors and millwork) Cost & Time - Currently has to be reliant on services team for new builds or fixing issues, leads to more cost and time. Bandwidth - Jesse himself doesn't have the time he would need to put into Allmoxy to get it to function. There wouldn't be anyone else able to fully set up his pricing and get this functioning the way it would need to in order for it to make sense.

engagements.title: Catalog Updates
engagements.body:
Best Choice.


On applied end products (whole category),

get rid of the Drawer Box Material and make sure it shows the Front Material attribute. Keep top three options (12 per sqft) Get rid of PVC options and add 3/4" white melamine (8 per sqft).

Applied End (wall tall and base)

Toe Face product: Get rid of Width and put in Length (make sure the max length is 108" in validation for Length). Make sure pricing formula works for Length by Height.

Get rid of all the "L" products.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

On cabinets,

For Construction Method, change name of top option to just say "Butt Joint Staples" and hide the second option.

For wall cabs, add the Construction Method attribute to all cabs. Test to make sure they are showing on all walls.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

On Closets,

For all Closet cabs, add the Construction Method attribute to all cabs. Test to make sure they are showing on all Closet units.

For all Closet cabs, add a option under Construction Method (only for closet units using overrides) called Cam and Dowel.

Replace Closet category images with the new images sent via email.

Replace Closet PRODUCT images with the new images sent via email (crop out the correct image and make sure it's square).

For all Closet cabs, have them default to the 5/8" Melamine option for the Box Material using the overrides.

For all Closet cabs, have them default to the 5/8" Melamine option for the BACK Material using the overrides.

On 5 and 4 drawer closet units, make the Drawer Height options match what's available for the 3 Drawer unit.

engagements.body: This is the first year renewal for Lane 17 Cabinet, Co. proceed to prepare data and engage the customer to execute a renewal meeting.

02/11/25 Retention Plan Meeting Context: Alex asked when his contract is up and I confirmed with him it will end as of March 10th. He wants to keep his data for 90 days so he can come back and potentially get back into Allmoxy. The goal of this meeting is to determine a gameplan with Alex to see what will be needed for him to start using the system in 90 days and also confirming that his access will be removed during the 90 days. Agenda: Pause timeframe - looking for 90 days Do you feel that you'll have bandwidth in 90 days? Anticipating more time available? What's left to complete within the catalog? How can we hit the ground running once the 90 days are up? Removing payment method as of March 10th (loose access after that) Scheduling a time to re-sync after 2 months of pause to see how bandwidth is looking and if we can plan to resume the project. Notes: Meeting recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/view/Lane-17-Allmoxy-Quick-Sync::01JKR8NYAZ435KQC9MSDPE0CNA Takeaways: Alex hasn't had the bandwidth to invest into setting up Allmoxy as he needs it to function. Alex learned throughout the last year that he and his partner, Jason, need to first define their catalog offering within Microvellum so they can then use this outline to match up Allmoxy. Essentially they put the horse in front of the cart and weren't ready to actually implement Allmoxy. New plan I've removed their payment method from their account so once the next charge date hits they won't be charged. I'll be reaching out to Alex in mid May to see how the backlog of work is coming along and if anticipates having the bandwidth to dive back into Allmoxy. Confirming with product how long the data will be stored if someone hasn't logged in or submitted a payment (believe this is 12 months)

Check-in Meeting (Catalog progress) 10/3/24 Agenda: Catalog progress How has the work been going? Any issues? Platform familiarity Feeling more comfortable since you've been building the catalog? What's next? Our services team is waiting on information to build out the door only product lines, correct? What's your timeline look like for being able to start using the system? Next Steps Share the information with me and I can get it to Juan/Aaron Schedule a touch base call for the end of the month Notes: Still has multiple projects on his plate. Door only products - could use sooner rather than later Get clarity from Juan - what information is needed for the doors.

engagements.body: Allmoxy - Meet with Sam

250 USD for the first month. 899 USD for the remaining months. Twelve-month contract agreement. 50-100 hours at $150/hour Alex is the owner/founder. Cleveland Ohio based and doing 80% custom repeatable and 20% fully custom. They do 0-1 million and have 6-10 employees. Their target customer is dealers. engagements.title: Build out Thermofoil Doors
engagements.body:
When a customer calls us for thermal foiled products, we typically need the following:

1) Door Style

2) Door Size for each door

3) Thermal Foil color choice (attached) need the full list and pricing on there

4) Do they want hinges bored? What type? How many? Hole placement? We provide hinges?

5) Color matched backs? Closest back? White back? Black back?

We also provide other thermal foil products.

1) 1/4 - 3/4 panels flat press 1 side all edges (1.5 inches wide by 96 inches long is the smallest)

2) 1/4 - 3/4 panels 2 sided no edges

3) 1/4 - 3/4 panels custom shapes and sizes

4) 1/4 - 3/4 panels full wrap (closest back, white, black, color matched?)

Currently we would like to offer:

1) 15-20 door styles

2) Ability to request a custom door style

3) Edge Profile default choice (1/16, 1/8, 1/4, 3/8)

4) Ability to add as many doors/panels as necessary

5) Ability to customize edge profile on any door (so default edge when door style is chosen, but can change edge on any door necessary and it overrides default)

6) Ability to change color/texture on a per door/panel basis.

7) Thermal foil color/texture automatically changes sqft pricing appropriately. (ie. solid colors are cheaper than gloss etc.)

engagements.body: Regarding email: Mountain Shadow Woodworks​- Contract Saving Renewal, sent on Tuesday, April 23, 2024 12:46 PM

Renewal 2024 Kenzi and Carl in attendance. Started running revenue/orders through the system in January of 2024. This is their first year with Allmoxy. Things have been ok this last year. it has been difficult because Carl feels as if the system is pretty complicated. Taken months to get setup. They have been with Allmoxy for one year now. It was about January when they started getting things figured out. I asked if there has been anything that has been a value add and he said not really. He feels like it's extremely difficult to ensure they have all the things put together correctly. Almost feels like they have to know how do a lot of programming and he is having to do a lot on his own. It seems very difficult to setup triggers, invoicing, etc. so they just want to use it for orders. Carl recognizes Allmoxy has a lot of features but they don't use them. They only use Allmoxy because it's an easy way for them to have people order from them. Would be ideal if they could pay for specific features instead of having to pay for it all. Essentially a SKU based subscription. Carl claims he hasn't heard from anyone in the year of signing up. He feels like he is a small little guy and feels like we maybe spend more time with companies that are bigger instead of the smaller companies. I looked through the emails and asked him if he received the email regarding the CS rep change and WTS. He said that he got the WTS email and must have overlooked the email.   Overall he wasn't very happy regarding his Allmoxy experience. He says he goes home at night and tries to figure out how to set things up. I re-ephmasized how important and valuable it would be for him to meet with Josh to setup some time to go over the things and pain points that he has experiencing. To allow for Customer Success to set up some trainings for him to see if there are other components within Allmoxy that he could utilize and overall have more value added to his jar than what he has experienced this last year. He is open to the idea. Feels like they could pay someone to design a website, etc. for cheaper. than what he uses Allmoxy for. Doesn't like that as his revenue increases his price increases. I let him know that it's our pricing model. He also was unhappy that we continue to charge for their instance once their agreement is up.  He brought up cancellation and asked what that process looks like. I encouraged him to meet with Josh first before he commits to cancelling and he agreed to it. We are keep pricing the same as they have just started running revenue through the system. Staying at $699 for this next year. I will connect Josh and Carl together and set a task for myself to follow up with Josh post the two of them meeting. @Josh Baker for visibility. If we could set up some re-occuring meetings with him it could be a great value add or else I think we might lose them. @Madison Theisen in case you find value in meeting with Carl prior to Josh returning. @Broc Hill for visibility. Would you like this to be moved to "considering cancellation" or remain in contract sent?

12/19/25 - Implementation meeting - https://app.fireflies.ai/view/Meeting-with-Stanley-Sommer-from-Evolve-Elements::01KCPM42BYKZWG1WSVAX3521YA Agenda: Stanley's agenda items - pricing help? Notes: Meeting Summary This meeting involved Stanley Sommer, Carson Ward, and Aaron Dundas discussing the setup, pricing, and product configuration for Rugby’s exclusive Allmoxy portal, specifically related to five-piece door panel materials and product visibility. The team focused on simplifying the setup, eliminating unnecessary product cloning, improving maintainability, and ensuring pricing logic and shipping configurations were in place. Rugby's operational requirements and regional pricing needs were central to the conversation. Key Takeaways Important Discussions Product Setup for Rugby: Focus is on creating a Rugby-exclusive product catalog in Allmoxy. Rather than cloning multiple products, a tag-based approach will be used to manage product visibility. Tags such as “Standard Offering” and “Rugby Products” will control what each group of customers can view. Rugby will only see products tagged for them, and the standard catalog will remain unaffected. Quarter Inch Panel Material: Need to differentiate quarter-inch and three-quarter-inch panels for five-piece doors. Cost difference is minimal but still relevant for product configuration. Panel materials will match the color of stile and rail materials — no separate color selection. Pricing Configuration: Setup completed to reflect quarter-inch sheet pricing and sheet size. Updates made to pricing formulas to calculate square footage accurately using the correct material. Shared markup and waste percentage between quarter-inch and standard materials unless modified later. Custom Product Naming: Allmoxy allows customer-facing names and internal "machine" names for Mosaic integration. Stanley needs naming consistency with Mosaic but can still show simpler names to customers. User Experience Improvements: Worth’s door ordering setup used as a UX benchmark — largely praised for intuitive visuals. Recommendation to use images and visual cues (e.g., highlighted selections) to aid customer understanding. Technical Issues & Fixes No critical bugs reported, but several backend improvements were made: Added quarter-inch sheet pricing and dimensions into attributes. Adjusted pricing formulas to accommodate the new material without complicating maintenance. Demonstrated the correct approach to cloning products and applying customer visibility tags. Set up future-proof structure for potential Rugby pricing adjustments (via meta fields and multipliers). Decisions Made No need for full product cloning unless strictly necessary. Rugby will be restricted from seeing the broader catalog via tag-based visibility. Quarter-inch panels added as attributes with proper pricing and size data. Allmoxy’s internal and external naming system will be used to maintain Mosaic compatibility while keeping customer-facing names simple. Challenges or Concerns Rugby's preference for iframe integration on their website could delay deployment. Regional pricing differences may require more custom configurations in the future. Risk of catalog complexity increasing if Rugby expands regionally with varying offerings. Shipping logistics still under discussion; freight partners not yet finalized. Action Items Stanley to: Receive final materials list from Brandon. Enter remaining products and validate pricing. Add quarter-inch material values for Tafisa and any smaller sheet sizes. Begin preparing visual aids for ordering (attribute images from Mosaic). Carson to: Push Rugby to begin customer onboarding once Stanley confirms pricing setup is complete. Support Rugby in tagging their own products/customers on their end. Advise against waiting for iframe setup to begin ordering. Aaron to: Finalize configuration changes to pricing and material attributes. Support any cloning/testing for future Rugby-exclusive product needs. Provide guidance on implementing shipping weight calculations if UPS/FedEx Freight is selected. Next Steps Stanley to complete product entry and confirm pricing accuracy by EOY. Carson to begin follow-up with Rugby early January to prompt account setup and B2B link sharing. Test orders to be created for Rugby to validate pricing, visibility, and shipping methods. Explore UPS/FedEx Freight integration once a carrier is selected. Revisit catalog structure in Q1 depending on Rugby’s expansion or complexity in regional offerings.

Onboarding 7/17/24 Reviewed triggers? (no) Set up a labor process (need to do) Financial order settings (determine when your customers pay) Default checkout flow (use credit limit or pay before processing) If some customers refuse to do pay before processing, you can change their individual checkout flow Credit limit is extending a certain amount of money to place an order, and set up payment terms (pay when they ship or order is marked complete) You set those terms Default interest rate- if you are doing terms and they haven't paid by the end of the month, it attaches a fee. Daily is every day something is past due, it attaches a fee Sales tax presence Where are you doing business, just Colorado or regional? 5K a year threshold- when you collect 5K in revenue from a state, you need to start collecting sales tax Bank info Stored bank info for internal use, it isn't really actively used but there to keep track of your bank/ banks. Statement editor (credit limit): goes out to your customers at the end of every month if they have an outstanding balance. Overhead management can be tracked here: lease payments, etc. Go to order page, click on the customer to show dashboard If pay before processing, it will just show their order history If there are credit limits, they can log in and pay from here (or you can do an offline payment- customers don't have access) Could be a walk in, pay in cash, or use square. Refund payments (demo) Undo transaction (transaction history report, then refund that payment on your stripe dashboard) Sales tax report (demo) A lot of customers file sales tax quarterly You would select the state and filter the dates- it will show what you owe to the sales tax commission Helpful report for knowing how much you need to pay in taxes Financial integrations (he uses QBO?) We recommend using the export invoices queue function This will get invoice information out of Allmoxy with an export you can use Transaction Pro or Sassant to map the Allmoxy export to QB (which we can help with- typically a one time set up) The more manual route is using the Export Transactions Queue (while having QBO pulled up) and reconciling payments Notes & questions Is there something bad about 3500 Credit Limit and 7500 order limit? They can place an order up to 3500, if they pay it down they can start another order. They can keep placing orders as long as they aren't verified. Wont ship anything until they have paid down their credit limit (if they are maxed out) Does the Status to Export Sales Order matter if it is none? Should he have the default status to charge customers be something other than Shipped if he is doing terms? Make it verified, because if we do it at ordered- there is no. Trigger at verified that says you have to pay 50% of invoice total for us to start the order. Have a trigger set up when payment has been made. Trigger when completed saying remainder of balance is due, or receive interest charge at end of month. (non paid invoices will be charged x amount at the end of the month) Shipping report will also tell him if there is an outstanding balance. For offline payments, why don't I see a credit card number? Is it just the ref #? They do 50% down, and 50% when it is completed (what is the best way to do this with triggers)? How do you ensure the customer pays the 50%. Put in trigger that they will get a finance charge after X amount of days (or at the end of the month) ACH payments (turned on) he wants his customers to be discounted if they want to pay with ACH Stripe processing fee, if they want they can send a physical check or use ACH (TRIGGERS, let them know stripe charges a fee, encourage ACH)- possible? (Michael actually pays the stripe fee from what he gets) 50$ he would get 48$ Don't encourage ACH. If he wants to not pay fees for stripe he can take check or cash payments. Sassant or Transaction Pro  (send info to Michael). He wants a Design category/ product (eventually) Design product fee for him to go to their house and build a design for them.

CS Onboarding Playbook Is this a VIP/Legacy customer?(If you're unsure check with leadership) No Is our Services team being utilized for this build? Yes, Services owning entire build Who is the main POC within the customer? Michael Ginzel Confirm the customers desired Outcome for using Allmoxy Automation Capabilities Notes: Online storefront, Mozaik export When is the customers goal launch date? 07/31/2024 Notes: ASAP, he took a few weeks to get necessary info to Juan What cadence of meeting schedule did you set with the customer? Notes: Weekly or twice a week Ask the customer to define their benchmark for success Online storefront, automation, Mozaik exporting, running orders, ease of customer use What Software(s) does the customer have? How will Allmoxy work with these softwares? Mozaik, Quickbooks Is the customer looking to fit Allmoxy around an existing ordering system or is this their first?(Utilize your Services Rep to more deeply understand how this impacts the catalog build.) Notes: New system Is the customer letting you drive the meeting and follow an agenda or do they want to drive and take charge of meetings? Either can be okay, but dependent on the customers approach to onboarding you will need to pivot your approach to working with them. Notes: He will let me drive, but a mix of both sometimes Any initial concerns with the customer and their ability to launch(personnel, resources available, understanding of product, etc?) Notes: Michael took a while to get services info to Juan, other than that- no.

7/8/24 onboarding meeting with Michael Address the resource allocation, that should be done after launching. Present category/ tagging solution (use verbiage in welcome email trigger that says please give us 24 hours to verify your account and give you access to our products) You will have to select Three Creeks or another company to see this on your end How an order moves through Allmoxy What is your current workflow? Does everything manually, goes onto distributors website, create online orders for materials after he counts them out on Mozaik. Manually types in those orders. Personally hands cabinet manufacturers blue prints. They ship all doors and drawers, he sprays them all. Has all hardware and material shipped here. He builds the cabinets. He hires a moving company or just rents a moving vehicle. I will do a test order There is an expected workflow in Allmoxy Bid --> Ordered --> Verified --> In progress --> completed --> shipped When an order is verified, it is locked (customer can no longer make changes) SHOW TRIGGERS AGAIN Have Michael do a test order Show Production Lines and Work Schedule Report (easy way to see jobs in verified status) He has some production lines set up, make sure the products are associated with those production lines (products, product info, associate with a production line) You can start jobs for each production line --> moving them to in progress (which will drop off from the report) It will show you a start by date and a ship by date (based off lead time) From there, you can mimick what happens on the job floor in Allmoxy by using the scanning station Shipping report Once an order is completed, you're ready to get those out the door. You're looking ahead. It shows you what method is being used, company name, etc. Shipping Methods Notes Hasn't figured out the margin stuff yet Has homework to do. Didn't set up tracking. Onboarding meeting 7/1/24 with Michael Tags These are ways you can group customers together for a certain purpose These can be referenced in triggers and price adjustments Ex. you have a group of customers that are developers, and they get a certain discount. You can give this group of customers a "developer" tag on their company profile that can then be referenced later. You can also put tags on products How do you think you might group certain customers together? Price Adjustments Do you have customers that are priced differently than others? Why? Use price adjustments to achieve this Say you have a customer that is your oldest and most loyal customer, you always give them a 10% discount no matter what. Price adjustments are basically discounts or surcharges that can be applied to customers, groups of customers, or products. They are adjusted PER ITEM, not total order amount Accumulation For when there are multiple price adjustments competing with one another If one discount has a higher priority than the other, the highest priority will override the other discount Ex. if you have a new customer discount and a summer sale discount going on at the same time, you would want the new customer discount to have a higher accumulate than the other. Tip: Use the Always setting, so you know if you are discounting or surcharging every time. You can also discount customers or products with certain tags Triggers How are you currently interacting with customers? Is it manual calls, emails, etc? Triggers can automate that process for you Notify you, and your customers of something happening in Allmoxy Triggers to edit: 1, 6, 12, 16, 18, 19 Does he want to be notified of a bid? Or an order? Homework Edit the triggers, keep them deactivated for now Start thinking about how you want to use price adjustments- write down some ideas Notes Material cost and markup is what makes up our catalog Working on adding cabinet line to catalog that is a standard cheap cabinet. That will be 1 product line he offers directly to one contractor. Doesn't want competitors to see their pricing, use tags to restrict. Wants to see highest price, or just a 24 hour notice. Doesn't even want them to access the catalog until verified. Distribution method, he sent over pricing to Juan.

engagements.body: Spoke with Bud and let him know that he can continue building his catalog while the pause is in place. He was very excited and appreciative of this.

Pause Request 9/30/24 Bud reached out saying that their sales have dropped throughout August and September which lead to his leadership asking his team to cut all unnecessary expenditures. He'd prefer to have a temporary pause (3 months) so they don't lose the work he's completed so far and that they can move forward with leveraging Allmoxy. At this time it seems to be an expense they can't afford. Bud's original email: "So, company sales took a downturn in August. Everyone thought that we would see a rebound in September. Well, that has not happened yet, and management is a bit anxious. I have been asked to suspend any expenditures that I possible can at this point in time.We need to pause or terminate our Allmoxy account as soon as possible. Of course I would rather suspend the account and let it be dormmate until such time that we could reactivate. Hopefully, that will be the first of year. I’m assured that the Allmoxy format is seen as a viable part of the business going forward, but now is a time for immediate cutbacks. The option of complete termination is something that I and the management team do not want to pursue. The likelihood of the company starting from scratch in the future is not likely to happen. Can you reach out to the powers that be at Allmoxy and respond to this email with a course of action that we both can abide by. The suspension of billings needs to be immediate. As in end of business today. If you can make that happen the team at Wedgewood will be very grateful. Please reach out with any questions regarding this request." I've responded to Bud by including Mekenzi and Broc so they can help determine an appropriate plan of action with hopes we can get them reactivated at the beginning of the year as Bud mentioned. @Broc Hill @Mekenzi Falslev for vis.

Onboarding Meeting Notes Q2 2024 Jeff Jennewein 5th Meeting 5/15/24 Agenda: Invoicing (Financial/Account Overview) Triggers - Use triggers or account settings to send invoices to customers If they're paying through the system you can link them back to their account page to submit payment. Leverage Tags if you need to send to multiple people Order Settings - Set up your terms and conditions for your order settings Output page - Customize your invoice to show exactly what you want Export - Export invoice queue for invoice movement into Sage Pricing You'll need to review this with Juan - He's out on Paternity leave for this week and next. If you can share examples of your pricing questions I can pass these along to my team, otherwise we'll need to wait for Juan. Your Agenda items What questions do you have? Next steps determine how close the pricing is working and either schedule a training session with our team or wait for Juan's return. Work on the output pages - Invoice, packing slip, etc Follow up on any other items Notes: Question - on pricing - need to be able to match their cv pricing in Allmoxy (how can they do this) Package video from Juan - PKG file Allmoxy master custom pkg file - should be able to upload into CV Found a restriction - version of CV 2021 Tried it in CV 2023 Perametric pricing - in CV right now. 4th meeting 5/2/24 Agenda: Financial settings Have you given more thought to how you, Bud, and the accounting team would like this to operate? Payment Processing Stripe - shared the incorrect link - we're 2.9% across every card type. Authorize.net- would need to connect to whichever processor you'd prefer. Simple Pay - Payment would have to take place outside of Allmoxy. Paperwork Allmoxy export orders to sage - if we use stripe or auth then customer's pay through Allmoxy. If using simple pay then customers would order through allmoxy and receive the invoice and link to pay once the orders are exported into Sage. (issue here is the delay in export time - Ex: customer could submit Friday but you don't export until Monday so their order doesn't move at all.) Credit Lines vs. Pay before Processing This flow will also impact if we're offering credit lines or making individuals pay before you're starting. If we're paying through Allmoxy then customers credit lines or lack of would need to be managed here. If payments aren't managed then customers could see large overdue balances unless you're also updating their invoices on our end. Next Steps Continue to discuss internally how you'd like this to flow. Determine a deadline of when this decision needs to be made by. Meeting next week to discuss catalog progress and automations (triggers, price adjustments, and tags) Notes: Using Sage Version: Sean sitting for Laura, she wasn't able to make it. Next weeks meeting will be circling back on the topic of Sage/Pay Simple (financial settings) May 8th we'll check in on the catalog build and discuss triggers, tags, and price adjustments 2nd Meeting 4/17/24 Agenda: Pay Simple & Sage Questions How does Allmoxy calculate sales tax? We have a lot of other major changes going on currently, and want to focus on those." How much is the customers monthly subscription?
