Title: Allmoxy Kick Off Call Date: Mon Aug 25 2025 16:45:00 GMT-0400 (Eastern Daylight Time) Participants: bobby@allmoxy.com, joshb@allmoxy.com, information@craftedcabinet.com Transcript: See full transcript Audio: Listen to audio Duration: 15 mins Overview - Sean Carroll's emergency situation limited his participation; Bobby Lewis introduced Josh Baker as the customer success representative for Allmoxy integration support. - The initial product launch focuses on The Christie vanity in 21-inch and 24-inch widths, both 24 inches deep, with a B2C business model differing from typical B2B clients. - Christie vanity will be available only in walnut, rifts on white oak, and regular white oak finishes—no additional options will be offered. - A shared Google Drive folder has been organized by Sean containing critical product documents, including cut sheets and pricing, which incorporates shipping costs. - Vendor contact information for door ordering and shipping details, including weights and pallet dimensions, will be added to the Google Drive by Sean. - The implementation strategy recommends The Christie as the pilot product for Allmoxy, with plans to replicate the setup for additional products later. - A one-hour training session is set for Sean to learn about product duplication and making minor adjustments post-integration. - Dropdown menus will be used for product configuration to mitigate pricing errors, with a custom size upcharge of 20% for dimensions from 74 to 78 inches. - An empty Allmoxy instance will be initiated for unique product configurations, ensuring clarity in customer ordering and account creation processes. - Future development plans include the readiness of additional products, Giselle and Horizon vanities, awaiting finalization of websites and related options. Notes 📋 Emergency Meeting Context & Introductions Sean Carroll had an emergency come up and could only participate for 10 minutes. Bobby Lewis introduced Josh Baker as Sean's customer success representative who will handle all Allmoxy integration and engineering coordination. Meeting was being recorded as noted by Bobby. 📦 Product Overview & Business Model Sean's company is launching vanities initially, followed by cabinet doors later. Business model is B2C which differs from Allmoxy's typical B2B clients. Main product focus is The Christie vanity available in 21-inch and 24-inch widths, both 24 inches deep. Christie will only be offered in walnut, rifts on white oak, and regular white oak - no other finishes. 📂 Documentation & File Structure Sean organized shared Google Drive folder with product information including photos, cut sheets, elevations, and pricing. Pricing includes shipping to avoid complications during ordering process. Sean plans to add vendor contact information for door ordering and shipping details including weights and pallet dimensions. 🛠️ Implementation Strategy & Next Steps Josh suggested starting with The Christie as the pilot product, then duplicating the setup for other products. Plan includes one-hour training session for Sean to learn product duplication and minor adjustments. Sean mentioned having additional products ready: Giselle and Horizon vanities with pricing built but websites not yet created. Sean's next development phase includes adding stain selection options and related photography. ⚙️ Technical Configuration Decisions Product configuration will use dropdown menus instead of free-text input to prevent pricing errors. Custom sizing option discussed with automatic 20% upcharge for sizes between 74-78 inches. Bobby confirmed starting with empty Allmoxy instance due to unique product differences. Website integration will include direct link to Allmoxy for customer ordering and account creation. Action Items Sean Carroll Complete uploading all Christie vanity documentation to Google Drive folder and notify Josh when ready Organize cut sheets and ordering forms in detailed folder structure for engineering team Provide vendor contact information for door ordering and shipping logistics Add product weights and pallet dimensions for Old Dominion shipping Josh Baker Send contact information email to Sean immediately after meeting Coordinate with engineering team to begin Christie vanity product build once documentation is complete Schedule one-hour training session for Sean on product duplication and configuration adjustments Bobby Lewis Support Josh with Christie product implementation and engineering coordination Guide Sean through additional Allmoxy platform elements after product base is established

Kick off call 8/25 with Sean & Bobby Relationship between CS and implementation Build type would be hybrid/ asynch (explain what that is) Who are his end customers going to be? What products are going to be offered? To start, are we doing the vanity sinks from your website? How are you currently pricing your products? Do you have any reference material that I can share with our engineers? (excel spreadsheet, cutlists, pricing information, product offering, etc)? Meeting Summary The meeting focused on the kickoff and setup for Sean Carroll’s vanity product line in Allmoxy. Due to an emergency, Sean had to leave early, so Bobby and Josh aligned on next steps. Sean is currently preparing assets including pricing, elevations, 3D renderings, and cut sheets for various vanity models—starting with “The Christie.” Josh Baker will be the primary Customer Success Rep coordinating technical integration. The team agreed to start with one product (The Christie) and use it as a template for others. Key Takeaways Important Discussions Sean has: Pricing completed for several vanity models. Started on 3D renderings and is mailing out product samples. Begun populating a shared Google Drive with necessary materials for each product (photos, elevations, cut sheets, and order forms). Primary product to start with is The Christie vanity (24"W x 24"D). Products will be offered in limited finishes: walnut, rift-sawn white oak, and standard white oak. The offering is direct-to-consumer (B2C), differing from Allmoxy’s usual B2B clients, but should be manageable. Technical Issues & Fixes Product listings will use dropdowns for dimensions and options to prevent manual input errors (e.g., no entering "26” when 24” is standard). Sean requested the ability to handle custom size pricing via a percentage add-on (e.g., +20% for custom range). Josh recommended starting with an empty Allmoxy instance due to product uniqueness. Website pricing includes shipping to avoid complications. Decisions Made Start with building “The Christie” in Allmoxy. Engineer will build version 1 of the product, then review with Sean before duplicating to other models. Sean will organize the Google Drive further and populate it with all assets and cut sheets. Engineering team will provide Sean with training on how to duplicate products and make edits in Allmoxy. Challenges or Concerns Need for detailed technical data: pallet weights, dimensions, vendor contact info, and photos. Importance of clearly organizing assets in Drive to minimize back-and-forth or misinterpretation during setup. Sean will be responsible for adding the remaining products (e.g., Giselle, Horizon) once Christie is finalized and system is understood. Action Items Sean Carroll Complete upload of all Christie assets to Google Drive (cut sheets, order forms, pricing, elevations, renderings, etc.). Organize product folders clearly with naming and subfolders by dimension/variant. Confirm product website aligns 1:1 with what will be available in Allmoxy. Provide pallet specs (weight and dimensions) and vendor contact information. Josh Baker Email Sean contact details and initiate Christie project with engineering. Coordinate training on product duplication/editing once Christie is built. Support Sean with implementation and clarification needs throughout the build. Engineering Team (via Josh) Begin setup for The Christie in Allmoxy. Provide walkthrough or documentation/training video once version 1 is complete. Next Steps Sean will give Josh the go-ahead once all Christie materials are uploaded and organized. Josh will notify the engineer to begin setup immediately after. Once The Christie is reviewed and finalized, Sean will move forward with additional products using the same structure. Schedule training session for Sean on how to duplicate/edit products in Allmoxy after initial build is complete.

Title: Allmoxy Scope Call - Crafted Cabinetry and Millwork Date: Wed Aug 20 2025 12:15:00 GMT-0400 (Eastern Daylight Time) Participants: bobby@allmoxy.com, information@craftedcabinet.com Transcript: See full transcript Audio: Listen to audio Duration: 18 mins Overview - Sean Carroll targets $1.8 million in revenue for next year with Bobby Lewis's support to achieve business growth. - Public ordering feature allows customers to configure products without logging in; accounts needed only for saving orders, aligning with Sean's customer interaction needs. - Allmoxy integrates with KCD software for cabinet design, providing end-to-end automation, surpassing basic Shopify order capture capabilities. - Direct vanity linking to Allmoxy configurators from Sean’s B2C website is complicated; alternative to hyperlink to main order page discussed. - Customer workflow established: view options on Sean’s site, click 'Place Order' to access Allmoxy configurator for vanities like Kaden 60-inch double sink. - Subscription agreed at $250/month for initial volume with $100/hour engineering support, aiming $50k-100k in initial revenue. - Crafted Cabinet instance URL is craftedcabinet.allmoxy.com; custom domain available for $20/month, decision made to start with standard URL. - Bobby confirms engineering capacity for immediate project start; contract sent via PandaDoc for quick onboarding. - Kickoff meeting to be scheduled with customer success rep and engineering team to align on implementation strategy. Notes 📈 Initial Discussion & Goal Setting Sean Carroll aiming to reach 1.8 million in revenue next year with Bobby Lewis's assistance Discussion about busy business operations and growth trajectory 🛠️ Public Ordering Configuration Bobby demonstrated public ordering feature allowing customers to view and configure products without logging in initially Customers can see configurator but must create account before saving orders Sean confirmed this approach meets his needs for customer interaction 🔗 Software Integration Discussion Sean uses KCD software for cabinet design, Bobby confirmed Allmoxy integration capability Allmoxy provides end-to-end automation from order capture through production, including printing plans Platform offers significant advantages over basic Shopify accounts which only capture orders 🌐 B2C Website Integration Challenges Sean inquired about direct vanity linking from his website to specific Allmoxy configurators Bobby explained platform is B2B-focused rather than B2C, making direct product linking complex Alternative solution: hyperlink to main order page where customers select specific vanities 📦 Order Process Workflow Agreed on workflow: customers view vanity options on Sean's site, click 'Place Order' to access Allmoxy configurator Customers would select specific models (e.g., Kaden 60-inch double sink) and customize finishes/colors 💰 Pricing and Subscription Agreement $250/month subscription agreed upon for initial volume expectations $100/hour engineering rate for development and support work Sean's initial revenue targets: $50k-100k to start, with scaling expectations 🔧 Technical Setup Details Instance URL set as craftedcabinet.allmoxy.com Custom domain available for $20/month additional Sean opted to start with standard URL, may upgrade later 🗓️ Implementation Timeline & Next Steps Bobby confirmed optimal engineering capacity available for immediate start Contract sent via PandaDoc to information@CraftedCabinet.com Kickoff Title: Allmoxy Kick Off Call Date: Fri Dec 12 2025 16:15:00 GMT-0500 (Eastern Standard Time) Participants: bobby@allmoxy.com, joshb@allmoxy.com, crystalcabinetworks@hotmail.com Transcript: See full transcript Audio: Listen to audio Duration: 35 mins Overview - Implementation Start: Team will upload a structured product template to fast-track Almoxy setup. - Pricing Adjustments Needed: Current pricing model has gaps; accurate costs for materials and finishes are essential. - Payment Processing Choice: Client will use Authorize.net for payments, prioritizing security over convenience. - User Access Management: Multiple users will be added to Almoxy, ensuring appropriate roles and limited financial visibility. - Communication Plan: Written communication will supplement calls to address language barriers and ensure clarity. - Next Steps: Engineer to upload product template, with pricing details and Authorize.net setup needed by Monday. Notes 👤 Introduction of Josh Baker Josh Baker introduced as the Customer Success Manager for the client account and implementation process with Almoxy. 🔑 Login Credentials and Template Preferences Discussion on login credentials and access to product templates. Client interested in exploring the template catalog, preferring default clean slate templates over extensive customizations. 💰 Pricing Concerns Identified gaps in pricing formulas within the provided templates that need adjustments for accuracy based on client-specific costs. 📊 Product Catalog Focus Clarified that the product catalog display will focus on the sales and order entry system rather than manufacturing software (Cabinet Vision). 🌐 Website Usage Plans Client plans to use the website primarily for product display rather than direct ordering, targeting local projects outside the website channel. ⚙️ Template Product Configuration Decision made for Almoxy engineer Aaron to push template products into the client’s instance and configure detailed pricing and dropdown options. 🛠️ Product Types Discussion Discussion on product types offered including doors, cabinets, and drawer boxes, with a commitment to incorporate accurate pricing. 💳 Payment Gateway Options Client prefers Authorize.net despite limitations; Almoxy to support Authorize.net setup. 📅 Active Invoices and Test Transactions Client has active invoices and work orders to process before year-end and wants to run test transactions. 🧾 Tax Rates and Shop Location Setup Setup of tax rates and default shop location for sales tax calculations discussed and partially configured. 👥 User Account Training Training on user account creation and permission assignment provided, indicating multiple users will be added. 📧 Next Steps Agreement Agreement to send client an email with a detailed list of pricing and product information needed for configuration. 🔄 Communication Challenges Concerns raised about communication challenges with the client, highlighting difficulties in understanding. ✉️ Need for Detailed Communication Acknowledgement that most communications may need to be handled via detailed emails or through other staff members. Action Items Bobby Lewis Coordinate with engineer Aaron to push the product templates into the client’s Almoxy instance Adjust payment gateway settings to use Authorize.net as preferred by client Send Dennis an email outlining all required product details and pricing information needed for configuration and implementation Josh Baker Guide Dennis through the implementation process and product catalog setup after templates are installed Assist in configuring financial settings, including tax presence and user permissions setup during the meeting and follow-ups Email client a detailed list requesting square foot pricing and product cost data to finalize pricing formulas Dennis Provide product cost data including pricing for doors, drawer boxes, finishes, and hardware to support template customization and proper pricing Obtain Authorize.net login credentials and transaction key from the payment processor team to enable payment gateway connection in Almoxy Set up user accounts and permissions for other team members who will access the Almoxy platform

Title: Allmoxy Demo - : CRYSTAL CABINET WORKS Date: Wed Dec 03 2025 15:15:00 GMT-0500 (Eastern Standard Time) Participants: bobby@allmoxy.com, crystalcabinetworks@hotmail.com Transcript: See full transcript Audio: Listen to audio Duration: 42 mins Overview - Onboarding Ahead: Crystal Capital Works to start with $417/month subscription for expected $500,000 annual volume. - Setup Fee: Estimated setup fee of $5,000 to $10,000 for customization and integration. - Demo Instance: Custom demo instance and Cabinet Vision catalog will be provided for initial setup review. - Order Management: Software includes order management, inventory control, and customer self-service features. - Automated Communication: Automated email triggers will improve customer interactions and reduce manual follow-ups. - Timeline for Launch: System aimed to go live for order processing this winter after signing agreement. Notes 🔌 Video Connection Issues Discussed video connection issues at the start but proceeded without video successfully. 📦 Crystal Cabinet Works Overview Crystal Cabinet Works, based in Minnesota, seeks streamlined software for inventory, scheduling, invoicing, and order management, replacing Microsoft Business Electric 5 due to complexity. Company serves both commercial construction and private residential customers with framed and frameless cabinets, cabinet care and cleaning services, and operates a factory in Louisiana. 🖥️ Allmoxy Customer Portal Features Bobby Lewis explained Allmoxy’s customer portal allowing customers to view order status, outstanding balances, and make payments securely via Stripe integration supporting cards and ACH, emphasizing security and convenience. Discussed alternative payment gateway authorize.net for credit card payments but without stored cards; Stripe preferred for security and stored payment info. 📊 Integration with QuickBooks Online System integrates with QuickBooks Online for seamless syncing of invoices and payments, including automated past due reminders via email triggers. Product configurator allows building custom cabinetry orders with instant pricing; expert consultation needed to define product catalog and pricing. 💰 Tax and Pricing Management Software handles automatic tax calculation based on customer location/zipcode and allows manual override for tax-exempt customers. Supports pricing adjustments per customer or product with discounts or surcharges. Customers can specify shipping method with shipping costs automatically calculated and included in orders. 📋 Order Management Features Order management on owner side includes viewing bids, in-progress and completed jobs, inventory allocation and purchase order creation linked with inventory levels. Bobby Lewis confirmed ability to import Cabinet Vision catalogs into Allmoxy for streamlined integration with existing manufacturing software. 🛠️ Customization and Template Features Software allows template creation and supports customizable dropdown menus for product variations, including construction methods and door types. Partial payments and deposit requirements configurable with automated payment request emails containing payment links triggered by order status or customer tags. 📧 Automated Customer Communications Triggers automate customer communications including order confirmation, payment receipts, and shipping notifications to reduce phone calls. Supports itemized invoicing for services like cabinet cleaning and care, with customizable product attributes and photos. 🎨 Branding and Pricing Model Company logos and branding customizable in the software interface via theme uploads. Pricing model based on monthly subscription variable on annual sales volume; estimated $417/month for $500,000 annual volume with a 12-month minimum, plus a setup fee for engineering services ($5,000-$10,000 range) to build product catalog and customizations. 📝 Agreement Process and Next Steps Agreement process: contract to be sent upon meeting end; instance setup and catalog import initiated on contract signature; demo credentials and access to software to be provided for team review. Client emphasized urgency to implement and ability to make quick payment upon receiving contract; expressed strong positive impression of software ease of use and potential for business growth. Action Items Bobby Lewis Send subscription agreement for $417/month based on $500,000 annual volume Provide demo access with sample login credentials for review Import Cabinet Vision catalog matching Crystal Cabinet Works' products into Allmoxy instance Assist in defining dropdown options and pricing customization after initial setup Guide and support team during software onboarding and setup process AA / Crystal Cabinet Works Review Allmoxy demo and template catalog provided Sign subscription agreement promptly to initiate setup and contract process Coordinate internal team to evaluate software features and product catalog fit Make payment upon receipt of contract to expedite implementation Reach out via email with any further questions during setup phase

Title: Allmoxy Demo - The Premier Hub Date: Thu Apr 03 2025 17:15:00 GMT-0400 (Eastern Daylight Time) Participants: bobby@allmoxy.com, cheneil@allmoxy.com, juan@thepremierhub.com, nathalia@thepremierhub.com Transcript: See full transcript Audio: Listen to audio Duration: 64 mins Overview The Product Demo and Requirements Gathering meeting for The Premier Hub's integration with Allmoxy featured Juan and Natalia from The Premier Hub, alongside Bobby Lewis from Allmoxy, who demonstrated their online sales solution tailored for custom cabinetry. The meeting began with introductions and an overview of The Premier Hub’s business model, currently 70% B2C and 30% B2B, with plans to enhance B2B sales. Key to the discussion was the need for Allmoxy's system to integrate with their existing Mosaic setup while allowing for streamline operations as The Premier Hub prepares to franchise. Bobby showcased Allmoxy's capabilities, including real-time pricing and automatic generation of Mosaic files upon order placement. Despite initial pricing concerns, adjustments were made based on their current sales volume, and a plan for a custom catalog was discussed to ensure operational clarity. Action items were assigned, including sending demo links and catalog templates, as well as a follow-up meeting to explore material options, ensuring both teams are aligned for effective implementation. Notes 🏢 Introductions and Company Background Juan and Natalia from The Premier Hub, a custom cabinetry shop in South Florida Bobby Lewis from Allmoxy demonstrating their online sales solution Juan mentioned they've previously had a meeting with Allmoxy about a year ago Juan explained they're seeking an online sales solution similar to what Allmoxy provides for DOT Cabinets The Premier Hub currently uses Mosaic for cabinet design and manufacturing Juan noted business is currently 70% B2C and 30% B2B, with goal to increase B2B to 45% 🔄 Business Model and Integration Needs Juan explained they need a system that integrates with their existing Mosaic setup The Premier Hub is planning to franchise their business model and partner with a Colorado company Juan described how they compete with Chinese/prefab cabinets by offering American-made custom cabinets Bobby confirmed Allmoxy can integrate with Mosaic, sending data directly to it Juan explained they currently use DOT Cabinets' website to quickly price cabinets Bobby demonstrated how Allmoxy can provide real-time pricing for custom cabinet sizes 💰 Pricing Structure and Implementation Juan questioned how the Mosaic integration works with Allmoxy Bobby explained Allmoxy handles business operations, ordering, payments, and inventory management Bobby explained that Allmoxy can send cabinet specifications to Mosaic for manufacturing Monthly pricing discussed: $1,200/month for $2M annual sales volume Juan indicated this was higher than expected (they pay $382 for Mosaic licenses) Bobby adjusted pricing to $500-550/month based on current monthly sales of $100,000 🛠️ Implementation Details Bobby offered to provide a catalog template that matches with a Mosaic catalog Juan emphasized wanting to start small ('less is more') with limited options Juan wants fewer material options than DOT Cabinets offers to streamline operations Bobby confirmed they can create a custom catalog matching Juan's requirements The integration would allow orders placed online to generate Mosaic files automatically Bobby explained implementation would include formula creation for pricing calculations 📊 Catalog and Product Management Juan asked if Allmoxy needs access to their Mosaic database Bobby clarified he would just provide a product library file that matches Allmoxy's catalog Juan explained his vision for a physical inventory of pre-cut cabinet components to reduce delivery time Bobby agreed the business model is viable and Allmoxy is well-positioned to support it Natalia asked about adding hardware products to the catalog (trash bins, spice racks, etc.) Bobby demonstrated how they could add products and have full control over their catalog 🔗 Final Details and Next Steps Bobby explained The Premier Hub's domain would be tph.allmoxy.com The system would include payment processing via Stripe (2.9% fee) Juan asked about showing credit card fees as separate line items on invoices Bobby will send demo links for Juan and team to explore the platform Bobby mentioned QuickBooks Online integration is coming soon Juan stated his franchise partner may also want to implement Allmoxy for their prefab cabinet lines Action Items Bobby Lewis Send demo link for The Premier Hub team to explore the Allmoxy platform Create and share a Mosaic product catalog file that matches the Allmoxy catalog Send subscription agreement for monthly payment Send pricing matrix showing volume-based pricing tiers Set up a follow-up meeting to discuss material options and dropdowns Juan Review the demo and catalog with the team to confirm it contains what they need Create a list of desired door materials and options for the catalog Connect the franchise partner with Bobby to discuss implementation for their stores Send profit and loss statements from previous year to Bobby for pricing considerations

engagements.body: Regarding email: Innovative Cabinetry And Design​- Contract Saving Renewal, sent on Monday, August 5, 2024 11:21 AM

Renewal 2024 Things have been going well. Jed finally feels like he has the shop set up that he has worked out the bugs. Now he just needs more customers, plans on hiring someone for sales to help selling the software. I let him know that Carson would be available for training should he decide to have his sales person get super familiar with the Allmoxy system. The biggest allmoxy value add has been getting materials in but then they got busy and sidetracked with some side projects. They are having a hard time going all in on getting pricing correct because of the amount of changes that are happening post importing into cabinetvision. Whether it's the customers fault or whether that's just their flexibility, like they have a lot of flexibility on their end and are not forcing people into what they have to offer. They will pretty much do anything for their customers. So that is probably the main hang-up with going all in. Jed sees the value in clicking a few buttons and sending the invoice and whether its charging a credit card or whatever, because he spends about 4 hours a week at least or more billing on his end but its just all the custom stuff that he does on his end that he can't really just bill for straight out of the box with Allmoxy. He mentioned that even if it was just getting some sort of a custom product created where he could quickly edit the final price or whatever before he ships the products. He said and maybe that's the easiest way to do it because he feels like he is getting close, and has been paying attention to what prices it's been shooting out for most of the jobs and compared to how I'm billing it, and it's right there, plus or minus a percent or two of where he would like to be. But he feels like that's ok, it's just the custom materials it added or once we get it into Allmoxy and he transfers the ORDX, and he transfers the RDX into cabinet vision, then they make changes if they add a cabinet or two, because he usually sends them assembly sheets out of cabinet vision, and then it comes back to him with the changes before he tests it. By doing that, it changes the price and he just doesn't want to lose out on all the money. So he essentially needs a quick way to get into their order, update their price without updating the product, like a different product and trying to make it work or it's just something custom say the add one panel, but they want to be boarded or grooved or they want, like a flower design cut in or something like that. He just needs to quickly edit their order to what he wants it to be before he ships it. Additionally, it would be making sure that he understands the back and forth between that and Quickbooks since that would be a whole different ballgame. He is currently using Quickbooks desktop. He said there is a lot of his business that does not run through Allmoxy because of his own personal jobs or commercial side of things. So he needs it to all run in one financial software type. So he needs to be able to import those invoices or import those accounts receivable or something into Allmoxy or Quickbooks so he can keep track of it. He said the payment will probably still end up going through QuickBooks or obviously if it's credit card, it will go through Allmoxy. But somehow getting those payments imported into QuickBooks so he can keep everything in one tab would be big. The ORDX he thinks is figured out and he has most of the import of the materials done, he still has some to import, but most of the materials stuff is figured out. With pricing finally leveled off a little bit, he thinks the next step is just trying to speed up the invoicing process. He is attending IWF and arrives Tuesday. I let him know he could stop by the booth and talk with you in person @Carson Ward. Or if you miss each other you could link up after the show. Forgive me if these notes don't make sense. I did my best to keep notes and keep up. You can always watch the fireflies if that helps. Let me know if you have any questions. Thank you!
